messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected at ingress (edge/gateway). Service: api-gateway-prod. Error types: 502, 504. Short window spike starting 2026-03-15T21:40:10Z. Paging oncall-sre and netops.

maya: seeing this in the eu-west-1 dashboards — 5xx rate jumped to ~28% for the last minute, baseline ~0.2%. Most errors are 502 from upstreams (model-proxy). Latency p95 hasn't increased much.

devin: confirmed. curl to health endpoints returns 502 intermittently. grabbing tcpdump now. logs show "upstream reset" and TLS session closed by server.

raj: if upstream is resetting connections we might be hitting a connection churn bug. are we seeing client_keepalive drops?

maya: yes, keepalive connection count on edge side dropped around the same time as kernel patch rollout to the NLB pool in eu-west-1 ~21:38Z. KV cache miss rate also spiked (prefix cache miss 18%).

oncall-sre: I'm taking lead. immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable circuit-breaker on the route 2) shift 30% traffic to fallback pool in other region 3) throttle ingress fanout to reduce concurrent upstream connections.

raj: preparing config change. applying reduced fanout (max_fanout: 8) to ingress route via `redctl` now. command:
```
redctl routes update api-gateway-prod --set max_fanout=8 --env prod --region eu-west-1
```

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for route config change (max_fanout=8) -> 10% of edge nodes. Monitor: 5m.

devin: tcpdump shows many RSTs from NLB IPs to upstreams, interval matches kernel upgrade window. suspect NLB kernel module causing SYN/FIN race.

netops: rolling back NLB kernel patch in eu-west-1 now. rollback initiated, ETA ~8m. will post progress.

support-bot: creating customer-impact ticket. Initial estimate: ~12 customers experienced elevated 5xx during spike. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/INC-2026-042 (tracking created). tagging account teams.

maya: after fanout change + circuit-breaker enable error rate dropped to ~6% on canary nodes. shifting more traffic to canary.

oncall-sre: increasing canary to 50% while netops completes rollback. keeping circuit-breaker thresholds conservative. added automatic fallback to lightweight-model variant for retryable requests.

deploy-bot: Route config now at 50% canary. No config deploy errors.

netops: rollback complete in eu-west-1 at 21:47Z. NLB kernel back on previous version. Monitoring for connection resets.

devin: post-rollback metrics look good — connections stabilized, upstream resets falling. 5xx rate back to ~0.6% across region.

maya: KV cache hitrate recovering. latency stable. will keep an eye for 10m.

oncall-sre: handing off follow-up to night oncall @tara. I'm still available if needed. Handoff notes: suspected root cause = NLB kernel patch -> connection instability -> upstream TLS resets -> ingress 502/504 spike. Actions taken: fanout reduced, circuit-breaker enabled, traffic shifted, NLB rollback.

tara: acknowledged. taking over monitoring and postmortem owner assignment. tagging devin as RCA owner.

support-bot: updated ticket INC-2026-042 with mitigation timeline and affected customers list. Notify: accounts and CSMs.

maya: quick reminder: collect tcpdumps from a representative node and edge logs for 21:35-21:50Z window and upload to S3 for RCA. path: s3://redwood-incident-logs/5076543210/

devin: uploading artifacts now. postmortem draft PR will be opened under infra/incidents with timeline + follow-ups. owning RCA.

oncall-sre: adding follow-ups: add automated detection for sudden keepalive drops, add NLB kernel change gating in canary for 30m, and run a chaos test on connection churn scenario.

maya: :thumbsup: good job everyone. closing active pager once tara confirms stable for 20m.

incident-bot: Incident update: status=Mitigated, mitigation_time=2026-03-15T21:47:30Z, severity=high -> monitoring. Next step: postmortem in 48h.
summary: edge ingress 5xx spike caused by NLB kernel patch -> connection resets; mitigated by fanout throttle, circuit-breaker, traffic shift, and NLB rollback. Postmortem owner: devin, handoff to tara.
